A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DECO research, with identifiable correspondences between methods, equations, experiments and figures despite the changed title and organization. All pages are readable. v1 ends with references and has no appendix; v2 includes Appendix A, which is included in this comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original COCO detection results, architectural ablations, query-slot visualizations and a synthetic generalization example in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains original detection experiments and adds segmentation results in Table 8 and deformable-convolution and FlashAttention experiments in Appendix A.

M1.justification: The central DECO decoder and Equations (1)–(3) remain unchanged under the InterConv terminology, and DECO+ already existed in v1. Procedural additions are localized: DECO-TinySAM replaces the mask decoder and repeats queries into two-dimensional features instead of reshaping them; Appendix A.1 introduces an optional DCNv3 replacement for the self-interaction depthwise convolution.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate COCO object detection, but v2 adds box-prompted zero-shot instance segmentation on COCO, substantially extending the prediction task. The synthetic unseen-instance-count scenario involving 24 repeated giraffes in v1 Section 4.4 and Figure 6 is removed.

E2.justification: v2 Table 1 adds evaluated comparators including DN-DAB-DETR, DINO-4scale, Stable-DINO, SpeedDETR, DDQ-DETR, Lite-DINO, Co-DETR, H-DETR, Focus-DETR and Rank-DETR. Conventional detectors previously compared with vanilla DECO are now compared with DECO+, while the separate vanilla comparison focuses on DETR. TinySAM and DETR equipped with FlashAttention are also new comparators.

E3.justification: New evaluation designs include segmentation prompted by detected boxes with mobile latency measurement, a ConvNeXt-B configuration for DECO+, and a PyTorch 2.1 timing comparison incorporating XFormers/FlashAttention while also timing DECO under the newer backend. The original vanilla DECO training schedule and timing over the first 100 validation images remain. Newly documented DECO+ settings do not establish that earlier experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The five original architectural ablations and query-slot analysis are retained. Appendix A adds focused tests of whether DCNv3 improves DECO+ and whether its efficiency advantage survives optimized attention. Segmentation examples are added, while v1's qualitative detection examples and synthetic giraffe generalization test are removed. These modify the supplementary analyses without replacing the central ablation program.

E5.justification: Neither version reports training-seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals or significance tests. Both retain the same practice of averaging FPS over the first 100 validation images; the new experiments introduce no uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Core DECO and DECO+ scores and the original ablation values are retained. v2 adds ConvNeXt-B results of 50.6 AP at 20 FPS, segmentation results of 41.4 AP/29 ms versus TinySAM's 41.9 AP/34 ms, and DCNv3 results of 41.5 AP/67 FPS. Shared baseline entries also change: Sparse R-CNN goes from 37.9 AP/20 FPS to 42.8 AP/23 FPS, and Deformable-DETR from 44.9 to 43.8 AP. These are revised reported entries, not established same-setting improvements. v2 also corrects the DECO+ R50 prose to 47.8 AP, already present in v1 Table 2.

T1.justification: The mathematical description of query upsampling, feature fusion, residual processing and pooling in Equations (1)–(3) is retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the new adaptations introduce no substantive mathematical derivation.

C1.justification: v1 centers its contribution on a query-based convolutional object detector. v2 presents InterConv as a more general attention-like decoder mechanism, explicitly claims that prior methods had not built a Transformer-style decoder with pure convolution, and extends its headline contribution to segmentation and mobile efficiency. The abstract and conclusion foreground existing DECO+ results instead of the original vanilla DECO results.

C2.justification: v2 adds a hardware rationale involving dynamic versus static memory access, explains why SAM's prompt and output tokens require repetition, and interprets segmentation results as evidence of transfer to another task. Appendix A.2 qualifies the efficiency discussion by acknowledging DETR's larger speedup with optimized attention. Existing ablation and query-slot interpretations remain, while the removed giraffe experiment's generalization discussion disappears.

D1.justification: v2 adds two code-access links, explains DECO+'s rescaling, concatenation and projection steps, specifies its training-size selection and 640-by-640 inference, and identifies timing software versions and XFormers. These largely expand documentation of retained methods and settings. Some details disappear, including v1's crop probability of 0.5 and explicit 150-epoch DETR baseline statement; encoder depths and widths are merely relocated.

R1.justification: The positioning expands from an alternative end-to-end detector to a convolutional decoder mechanism applicable across tasks. v2 explicitly distinguishes its query mechanism from SparseInst, contrasts its decoder focus with prior convolutional encoder work, and incorporates TinySAM, hardware, large-kernel convolution, deformable convolution and additional DETR literature. This substantively broadens the novelty argument beyond bibliographic updates.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are substantially rewritten around InterConv and segmentation. The approach now explains the interaction mechanism before constructing DECO, consolidating and relocating former subsections. Experimental discussion leads with DECO+, and dedicated segmentation and appendix sections alter the narrative substantially despite many retained technical paragraphs.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document from a two-column layout to the single-column ICLR format, redraws architecture diagrams and substantially expands the opening accuracy-latency plot. Main comparison tables are reorganized around DECO+, with additional metrics and rows. Segmentation and appendix displays are added, v1's qualitative detection and giraffe figures are removed, and retained ablation tables and query-slot graphics are relocated.

improvement.justification: The expanded detector comparison and Appendix A.2's optimized-attention control strengthen the relevance and credibility of the efficiency assessment. Additional DECO+ implementation details and code-access links improve reproducibility documentation, and Table 8 supplies evidence for the segmentation extension. The gains are limited by sparse segmentation training and mobile-hardware details, while some earlier generalization examples and training details are lost. Overall, the revision provides useful additional validation and clearer positioning without resolving all evaluation limitations.
